stem:
On the same flat page, lines $p$ and $q$ are each perpendicular to line $r$.

Which two claims correctly decide how $p$ and $q$ relate?

options.text: $p$ is parallel to $q$, because each is perpendicular to the same line $r$.
$p$ and $q$ make equal corresponding right angles with $r$, so $p$ is parallel to $q$.
Call line $r$ itself parallel to $p$ and stop.
$p$ is parallel to $q$ even if $p$, $q$, and $r$ are not kept in the same plane.

teacher.key_rationale: In the same plane, two lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel and make equal corresponding right angles with that reference. Naming r as parallel to p, or dropping the same-plane condition, miss the justification.
